samples.identification: ModManager 2.19.4 / WoM GTA mod installer, reconstructed CAPE image
evidence: Entry VA 0x4e0e3f reaches CRT startup and main 0x456e90, then WinMain 0x49f340. Admin-token inspection, game-path configuration, XML/resource handling and Sciter installer UI match the stated purpose.

WinMain IsDebuggerPresent at 0x49f3c1 selects a path bypassing its own elevation setup; this is not evidence of a malware analysis kill switch. OpenProcessToken, DuplicateTokenEx and CheckTokenMembership remain notable.

Hundreds of vehicle/character PNG assets and INSTALLER/UNINSTALLER HTML, CSS and TIS resources match GTA mod installation. The embedded PE at raw offset 0x1c2490 is Sciter. No alternative embedded attack payload was identified.
Installer APP.TIS lines 429-438 bind the log.php POST to a user clicking the exception-report link. Registry locations are Software\ModManager and game-installation settings.

UPX0 contains accessible unpacked code and .CAPE reconstructed-import data. UPX refuses to decompress it. The retained security directory does not establish an intact signature: osslsigncode reports missing/invalid signature placement and checksum mismatch. This is consistent with a reconstructed image, not proof of supply-chain tampering.

The source Triage overview contains UPX dump-on-OEP, packing and language-discovery findings, no recovered malware configuration. This explains the high score without establishing any of the malware families in the collector filename.
context_limits: Original packed installer, delivery chain and authorization history were not supplied. The supplied CAPE image is not a cryptographically verified vendor distribution.

Forager retries and web fallback could not retrieve modmanager.info: connection timeout. That unavailable site is not presumed benign. Available code/resources and sandbox details favor an installer false positive.

samples.identification: Obfuscated WSH-to-PowerShell loader for LxBaseRAT-compatible .NET RAT/stealer
evidence: Outer JS reconstructs a 421662-byte frame from shuffled fragments, uses XOR-rebuilt strings and a custom multistage byte transform. Arithmetic constants and fabricated library helpers conceal the code path.

set_Owner / Add / owner transitions bring collectorItem628 to 4. The payload then checks wall-clock elapsed time around a randomized WScript.Sleep (3700-5499 ms), requiring more than 3200 ms. This gates real execution against accelerated delays.

Recovered text is written as a temporary .ps1. Encoded COM names resolve WScript.Shell, Scripting.FileSystemObject and WbemScripting.SWbemLocator; Win32_Process.Create starts hidden PowerShell with policy bypass, followed by script/directory cleanup.

PowerShell section 08 copies the original JS into LocalAppData/CrashReportsaz/manifest.js and registers a hidden logon-triggered task through Schedule.Service. Task path names are configuration, not detection gates.

PowerShell runners load a decoded assembly through AppDomain reflection, select a static six-argument method by its signature, and pass the second decoded image with C:\Windows\Microsoft.NET\Framework64\v4.0.30319\MSBuild.exe as target.

Stage 1 is an 82432-byte RSG_UnityApp DLL. CSheader.DispatchContextualModulePipeline, _Spawn, _Prep, _Reloc, _WriteImage, _PatchPeb and _Launch implement a remote-image staging and activation pipeline.

Stage 2 is a 599040-byte assembly LX_PYLD_05E1C833. Main token 0x06000153 reconnects through _allHosts. Send token 0x0600015b writes a command byte, four-byte size and body to the peer stream, then flushes it.

Method token 0x06000011 reads browser Local State JSON, obtains os_crypt.encrypted_key and Base64-decodes the key. Other paths enumerate browser/wallet/messaging stores and decrypt Firefox logins through an embedded NSS helper. GetAsyncKeyState token 0x060000f1 is polled; screen capture calls CopyFromScreen and responses use the common sender. These corroborate RAT and credential-theft capabilities beyond a family label.
samples.coverage_limit: Two suspicious outer-file concealment detections are justified. Custom reconstruction is not automatically decoded by the scanner, so persistence, injection and theft in the recovered stages are absent from the outer-file traits. The independently scanned RAT stage retained eight hostile behavior findings. No duplicate convictions were added to inflate the classifier.

evidence: Archive contains only package.json, a 60-byte README and the 120-byte index.js helper. The helper only prints the npm search URL; no dependencies are declared.

postinstall creates a directory with mktemp -d, writes a generated manifest whose name contains openssl rand --hex 2 output, and runs npm publish $d. It finally removes the temporary directory. This uses the installing account's npm publishing authority, conditional on credentials/network availability.

Description contents are the fixed literal foobar. No environment harvesting, credential-file read, arbitrary external exfiltration endpoint, recursive propagation or payload download occurs in this version.

The documented search helper does not explain a package installation publishing a new public package. The proof-of-concept name and harmless published contents qualify the impact but do not make the install-time account action expected. This likely explains collection by Aikido.
context_limits: No explicit user consent to registry publication was supplied. Authorized laboratory execution is possible but unestablished.

The npm search URL is documentation, not a payload dependency; forager rejected its URL format and browser fallback could not fetch it. The exact predecessor 1.0.18 was recovered and its obfuscated publication behavior was checked.
samples.coverage_gap: One suspicious objective is supported: install-time temporary-manifest creation plus registry publication. OpenSSL random generation, temporary file writes, process/package-manager execution and cleanup remain notable. A second suspicious/hostile behavior would require inventing theft, evasion or propagation, so the requested minimum cannot be met honestly for this version.
